A local council is considering building a passenger terminal at a port so that it can benefit the large cruise ships that dock there. It undertakes a cost–benefit analysis. What would be included as an external cost in the local council’s cost–benefit analysis?

options.A: the cost of a ticket for a passenger to travel on a cruise ship
options.B: the cost of fuel to operate the cruise ships
options.C: the costs paid by cruise ships when they dock at the port
options.D: the cost to a fishing fleet of relocating to another port

questions.questionText: What is marginal cost?

options.A: the difference between the total cost of producing n units and n – 1 units of output
options.B: the difference between the average variable cost of producing n units and n – 1 units of output
options.C: the difference between the average total cost of producing n units and n – 1 units of output
options.D: the average fixed cost of producing one more unit of output

questions.questionText: What would not be classified as structural unemployment?

options.B: a coal miner whose mine closes because of increased use of solar power
options.C: a fruit picker who cannot find work in the winter months

What is an important assumption of Monetarism?

options.A: Fiscal policy is more effective than monetary policy in reducing inflation.
options.B: Long-term unemployment results from deficient demand.
options.C: The interest elasticity of investment spending is low.
options.D: The velocity of circulation is stable.

questions.questionText: According to Keynesian theory, how will an increase in autonomous spending affect the value of equilibrium income?

options.A: Income will increase by an amount equal to the value of autonomous spending.
options.B: Income will increase by an amount greater than the value of autonomous spending.
options.C: Income will increase by an amount smaller than the value of autonomous spending.
options.D: Income will not increase as a result of autonomous spending.

questions.questionText: Statement 1: A market economy is inherently unstable and the government must play a stabilising role through monetary policy and fiscal policy. Statement 2: The economy will always return to its equilibrium rate of output and unemployment and as a result long-run aggregate supply is vertical. Which row correctly attributes these statements to Keynesian and Monetarist theories? statement 1 statement 2

options.A: Keynesian Keynesian
options.B: Keynesian Monetarist
